plain: Official notice; also a court's authority to hear a case

webster.text: Judicial notice or knowledge; the hearing, trying and determining of a cause or action in court.

more.text: In law, an acknowledgment or confession; as in fines, the acknowledgment of the cognizor or deforciant, that the right to the land in question is in the plaintiff or cognizee, by gift or otherwise; in replevin, the acknowledgment of the defendant, that he took the goods, but alledging that he did it legally as the bailiff of another person who had a right to distrain.
A badge on the sleeve of a waterman or servant, by which he is known to belong to this or that nobleman or gentleman.
Knowledge or notice; perception; observation; as the cognizance of the senses.

example.quote: But this doctrine of concurrent jurisdiction is only clearly applicable to those descriptions of causes of which the State courts have previous cognizance.
